refined_trace: frame_retriever returns the full geometry problem at 37.5s in frame_37.50.png with top relevance_score 0.7089, and the same diagram also appears at 33.5s and 26.0s. OCR on these frames (avg detection confidence 0.9725) reads: "P, Q, R are centers of arcs that pass through O, the center of the circle" and "If \overparen{PQ} = \overparen{QR} = \overparen{RP}, what is the area of the shaded region?"

chart_analyzer on frame_26.00.png reports a large circle with center O, points P, Q, R on the circumference, radius OP labeled 6, and three symmetric red leaf-shaped regions. Its frame-level result also says the arcs centered at P, Q, and R pass through O and that these arcs bound the red regions, so the shaded part is the three red petals, not the central triangle.

Because OCR states \overparen{PQ} = \overparen{QR} = \overparen{RP} on the same circle centered at O, the corresponding chords are equal, so triangle PQR is equilateral. With OP = OQ = OR = 6 from chart_analyzer, O is the circumcenter of this equilateral triangle, so each central angle such as ∠POQ is 120°, giving chord length PQ = 2·6·sin60° = 6√3.

From that side length, area(PQR) = (√3/4)(6√3)^2 = 27√3. Also, each red petal is cut from a 60° sector of radius 6 centered at one of P, Q, R, so the three such sectors have total area 3·(60/360)·π·6^2 = 18π.

Since chart_analyzer identifies the red shading as the three petal regions bounded by those arcs around the central white triangle, the shaded area is total sector area minus triangle area: 18π - 27√3. Therefore the answer is A.
